newsitem.title: ITALY: INSTANT VIEW - Italy May CPI seen at 1.5 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Italy May CPI seen at 1.5 pct yr/yr.

text.p: The following are economists' reactions to preliminary consumer prices data from four sample Italian cities which indicate May CPI growing at 1.5 percent year on year and 0.2 percent month on month.
Economists in a Reuters survey had forecast on average a year on year rate of 1.5 percent and a month on month rate of 0.2 percent, compared with 1.7 percent and 0.1 percent respectively in April.
Alfredo Granata economist at Banca di Roma said, "I think the number is as expected and I think that this opens the way for an official rate cut by the end of the week."

Alessandro Fugnoli at Caboto said that he saw the possibility of a 75 basis point cut in the Bank of Italy's discount rate but said, "I think the Bank of Italy will remain cautious, they are in no hurry to cut rates."

Fugnoli added that the Bank would probably wait a little longer than this week, maybe until after the French elections or even next month's Italian inflation data, which he expected to to show a further slowdown.

Nomura economist Marco Pianelli said the improvement in inflation in the past three months supported a cut of 75 basis points, but he agreed that the Bank of Italy might be more cautious and cut only 50 basis points off the discount rate currently at 6.75 percent.

He added that there will be real problem if the Bank of Italy didn't cut on Wednesday after the remaining six cities release their data saying, "The improvement in the lira also rest on expectations that the Bank of Italy will cut."
Data from a fifth Italian city Naples, also due today, was delayed for technical reasons.
Six more sample Italian cities release their data on May 21 and final CPI data is due from national statistics institute ISTAT on June 4.
